findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A Windows user starts merge in the item's worktree with Forge v1.2.45, and refreshing the base changes the Forge pin.
The new chdir runs only in the selected release. The already-running v1.2.45 parent still waits in the worktree, and its `publish_on_exit` still calls `current_branch` if the folder remains. The base release's `src/forge/repo.py:993` and `src/forge/checks.py:63` show those older paths. If Git removes the worktree registration but leaves the locked folder, that parent replaces the successful merge with `git branch failed: not a git repository`.
The Windows workflow proof is also missing: the supplied proof list says no branch run exists, and `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:81` runs its Windows tests only on schedule or manual dispatch, not as a pull-request check.
Done-when item: forge merge started inside the item's worktree ends with exit 0 on Windows after it merges, and test_9 of the record-only test no longer fails on Windows; forge-next.yml's Windows jobs pass on the fix branch.
findings.title: Not done: Windows merge after a pin change and the Windows workflow

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A merge crosses a pin change from an already released Forge version.
The test's `_earlier_release(env)` call uses `tests/test_running_commands_follow_changed_forge_pin.py:23`, which copies the current source and changes its version rather than using the prior release's code. Its simulated parent therefore already contains both the new chdir and the new exit-flush guard. The added launcher can exercise an empty folder, but this test passes while the real v1.2.45 parent still fails after the merge, so it does not prove the named release-handoff behavior.
findings.title: Gate: the merge recovery test uses the repaired code as the earlier release

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A Windows developer installs Git for Windows with Scoop and runs the platform tests.
Scoop exposes `git.exe` through a shim while its Git installation contains Bash; see [Scoop's Git package](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Main/blob/master/bucket/git.json) and its [shim contract](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Shim). Resolving the shim path does not resolve its target, so this search checks the shim's ancestors, misses the installed `bin/bash.exe`, and skips test_9 despite usable Git Bash being present. The recorded allowance permits skipping this case only when no usable Bash exists, and the skip leaves the shared-history rule unchecked on that setup.
findings.title: Gate: test_9 skips when Git for Windows is installed through Scoop

why: The v1.2.45 release check fails on Windows in two places. First, forge merge run from inside the fix's worktree merges, cannot remove the worktree, then fails with 'git branch failed: not a git repository' (tests/test_merge_refreshes_behind_base.py test_2, all four cases; it passed on v1.2.44). Second, tests/test_record_only_failed_results.py test_9 runs a workflow step with bash, which on the Windows runner is the uninstalled WSL bash.
